what_its_for: Clorazepate is used to help relieve anxiety and nervousness. It is also used to help prevent seizures (epilepsy) when taken along with other seizure medicines, and to help manage the uncomfortable symptoms that can happen when someone stops drinking alcohol (alcohol withdrawal). It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines, which work by calming the brain and nervous system.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet unless your doctor says it is okay. Try to take it at the same time(s) each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause serious problems including withdrawal symptoms or more frequent seizures.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your condition, age, and other health factors. For anxiety, adults usually start with 7.5 mg taken two to three times a day, or 15 mg taken once at bedtime. For seizures, adults and children over 12 years old usually start with no more than 7.5 mg taken three times a day; your doctor may slowly increase your dose if needed. For alcohol withdrawal, your doctor will give you a special schedule that is carefully managed. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine, as combining alcohol with clorazepate can cause dangerous drowsiness, breathing problems, or even be life-threatening. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can make you very drowsy or dizzy. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, opioid pain medicines, muscle relaxers, or antihistamines, unless your doctor specifically approves them. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it may affect how the medicine works. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: very slow or troubled breathing, extreme drowsiness or difficulty staying awake, unusual mood changes or thoughts of harming yourself, confusion, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), increased seizures, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you notice signs of dependence such as needing higher doses to feel the same effect, or if you feel you cannot function without the medicine.
when_it_works: For anxiety relief, you may start to feel calmer within a few hours of taking your first dose. For seizure control, it may take a few days to several weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. For alcohol withdrawal, the medicine starts working quickly and is usually given over a short, carefully managed period. Keep taking this medicine as directed even if you feel better, and do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, including drowsiness, dizziness, and confusion, which can increase your risk of falls and accidents. Your doctor will usually prescribe a lower dose. Pregnancy: This medicine can harm an unborn baby and should generally not be used during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: This medicine is not recommended for children under 9 years of age for seizure use, and safety for anxiety in children has not been well established. Always consult your doctor.
